ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, directors, legal representatives, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories must undergo pre-engagement and closing-stage automated screening against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, PRC domestic export control and sanctions lists, and FATF high-risk jurisdiction lists. Enhanced due diligence is required for any politically exposed person, family member, close associate, or any person with adverse media or adverse local court/tax records. Screening results must be documented in an immutable audit log with the date, list version, matching algorithm, hit explanation, and compliance partner sign-off. Any positive hit triggers refusal, enhanced monitoring, or a suspicious transaction report to the PRC financial intelligence unit where applicable.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR National Market Entity Name Registration and Management Information System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE statutory name must be composed entirely of simplified Chinese characters and must follow the mandatory four-tier naming structure: administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or business characteristics, and legal form, in that order, ending with Limited Liability Company. Foreign-invested enterprises may use an English trade name for operational convenience, but the English name is not a statutory corporate name and may not replace the Chinese registered name. Phonetic transliteration of a foreign brand into Chinese is permitted under SAMR interpretive rules, provided the selected Chinese characters are distinct, non-misleading, and do not conflict with earlier registered rights. Traditional Chinese characters, English-only names, and names using prohibited or sensitive tokens are rejected unless ministerial approval is separately obtained.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration application in writing with the market regulation authority one level above the deciding registry within 60 days of the rejection notice, setting out the legal basis, the distinctive character of the proposed name, and evidence overcoming the stated conflict. In parallel, a fresh name reservation may be filed with a revised distinctive name. If administrative reconsideration fails, the applicant may bring an administrative lawsuit in a competent intermediate people's court within 6 months. For any sensitive token requiring ministerial approval, prior written consent from the State Council or the appropriate competent ministry must be obtained before refiling; the appeal process does not extend a valid name reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office and commercial mailbox arrangements are not permissible for this IVD manufacturing WFOE. The State Administration for Market Regulation requires a physical registered address supported by a lease contract, property ownership certificate, or land use right document. The municipal tax authority will reject a virtual address for VAT invoice issuance and payroll registration. The NMPA requires a physical licensed plant with controls and production equipment before issuing the Medical Device Production License. Furthermore, PRC banks require a pre-account-opening site visit and will not open RMB or foreign-exchange accounts, nor approve SWIFT LC or telegraphic transfer facilities, for a WFOE maintaining only a virtual mailbox. Use of a virtual office would trigger administrative deregistration risk and license invalidation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk is high, approximately 85% probability of an unannounced SAMR or municipal tax inspection within the first 12 months of registration for a newly formed WFOE in the medical device sector, and 100% probability of a formal NMPA on-site quality-system inspection before production license issuance. Banks also conduct site visits. The compliance checklist includes: physical lease or ownership certificate matching the registered address; utility bills; payroll and social insurance records; production equipment inventory; batch and quality-control records; environmental and fire-safety certificates; visitor logs; and a clear line separating office and warehouse or manufacturing areas. Failure to satisfy any item may result in name delisting, tax irregularity designation, bank account freeze, or production license suspension.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (Republic of China), Articles 128 through 156 (incorporation and share capital), Article 193 (board resolutions), Article 202 (board powers), Article 208 (chairperson), Article 218 (supervisors/auditors), Article 387 (registration applications), and Article 405 (foreign company registration). Foreign Investment Act, Article 7; Factory Management Act, Article 4; Medical Devices Act, Articles 18, 25 and 40.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan, operating through the One-Stop Business Registration Service.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Registration Application and Articles of Incorporation, as filed with the MOEA Department of Commerce.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is mandated for a Taiwan WFOE limited liability company under current Company Act. The Company nevertheless declares NT$10,000,000 authorized capital and a paid-up capital of NT$1,000,000, which will be deposited in a temporary escrow bank account, verified by a certified public accountant, and released only after issuance of the incorporation certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 2025-001 OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE COMPANY (TAIWAN WFOE LTD.) The Board of Directors of the Company, duly convened with a quorum present, and acting under Article 193 and Article 202 of the Taiwan Company Act and the Articles of Incorporation, unanimously adopts the following resolutions: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. The Board approves the issuance of 1,000,000 ordinary shares at par value of NT$10 per share, for an aggregate authorized share capital of NT$10,000,000. The Board confirms the subscription schedule submitted to the meeting and directs each subscriber to pay the full subscription amount into the Company's temporary escrow account at a licensed bank in Taiwan. The Board instructs the appointed certified public accountant to verify receipt of the subscriptions and to prepare a statutory capital verification report before submission to the registry. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board designates a licensed commercial bank as the principal banker of the Company. The Board authorizes the Chairperson and General Manager, acting jointly, to open bank accounts, sign account mandates, execute foreign exchange instruments, and operate SWIFT LC and TT wire payment rails. All wire transfers, disbursements, and loan commitments above NT$5,000,000 require two authorized signatories. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The Board adopts the premises identified as the Company's registered office in Taiwan. The Company Secretary is directed to file the registered office address with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and to display the incorporation certificate and tax plaque at the registered office. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The Board appoints the Chairperson and Managing Director, the General Manager, the Chief Financial Officer, and the Company Secretary, each appointment effective immediately and continuing until the next annual general meeting or earlier removal by the shareholders. The Board authorizes the Company Secretary to file the officer details, specimen signature cards, and any required corporate governance undertakings with the registry and tax authority. All resolutions are effective immediately and shall be binding on the Company and its officers. The Board directs the Company Secretary and the General Manager to execute all necessary documents, pay all filing fees, and take any corrective action required to complete the statutory incorporation, tax registration, and industrial licensing procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval and Company Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Investment Services, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Foreign Investment Approval Application through the MOEA Investment Commission online portal. Include a notarized certificate of incorporation and board authorization from the foreign parent, audited financial statements, and a certified power of attorney for the Taiwan agent. Submit the proposed Articles of Incorporation, clearly stating the Company's authorized share capital, business scope covering IVD microfluidic cartridge and immunoassay analyzer manufacturing, and the registered office address. After approval is granted, apply concurrently for company name reservation and business scope pre-review. Provide English and local-language notarized translations of all corporate records to ensure the registry can verify the investor identity, corporate existence, and lawful authorization of the proposed Taiwan entity.
required_dossiers: Notarized original certificate of incorporation of foreign investor
Audited balance sheet and income statement of investor
Power of attorney for local Taiwan agent
Corporate ownership and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA queries the foreign investment application, submit an explanatory memorandum and supplemental certified documents within 30 days. If the proposed company name is rejected, submit up to three alternate names and repeat the pre-screening procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit in Escrow Account and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan-licensed commercial bank and certified public accountant.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital escrow account at a licensed Taiwanese bank using the approved foreign investment certificate. Instruct the foreign parent to wire the paid-up capital in New Taiwan Dollars from an overseas bank, ensuring that the remittance identifies the share subscription purpose and the precise company name. Receive the bank passbook or electronic statement confirming the credit, and then engage a certified public accountant to verify the collection of funds and issue a statutory capital verification report. The CPA must confirm the source of funds, the absence of any withdrawal before registration, and the compliance of the capital contribution with the approved investment plan. The bank will apply enhanced due diligence because the entity is classified as a medium-risk IVD manufacturer under AML rules.
required_dossiers: Wire transfer instruction and SWIFT record
Bank account opening forms with specimen signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced AML due diligence, provide a source-of-wealth statement, corporate ownership chart, and client risk profile. If the capital transfer is below the approved amount, request a supplementary remittance and reissue the capital verification report.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application to Company Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), One-Stop Business Registration Service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation registration application to the MOEA Department of Commerce through the One-Stop Business Registration portal, attaching the approved foreign investment certificate, capital verification report, Articles of Incorporation signed by all subscribers, registered office consent, and directors' identity documents. Pay the official filing fee and request issuance of the company incorporation certificate and business registration certificate. The registry will conduct a statutory review of the company name, registered capital, business scope, and officer appointments. If the papers are complete and compliant, the registry issues the certificate and transmits the file to the local tax office for automatic tax registration. Any defect in the articles or officer consent forms must be corrected before the certificate is issued.
required_dossiers: Capital verification report issued by certified public accountant
Articles of Incorporation signed by all subscribers
Directors' proof of identity and specimen signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency notice, cure by filing amended forms and corrected dossiers within 15 days. If the registrar refuses registration on public-interest or name grounds, request a reconsideration in writing or file a new application using a different company name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Corporate Seal, and Permanent Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau (local branch) and Taiwan-licensed commercial bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the incorporation certificate, register with the National Taxation Bureau for profit-seeking enterprise income tax and business tax, obtain a uniform invoice number, and apply for tax withholding status. Open a permanent operating bank account in the Company's name and transfer the escrowed capital into it, presenting the incorporation certificate and the first board resolution authorizing the account signatories. Complete the beneficial ownership declaration and activate SWIFT LC and TT wire payment rails for import and export transactions. Execute banking mandate forms for the two joint signatories, and ensure that the Company's official seal and tax certificate are registered with the tax authority. The bank will perform a final AML screening before activating outgoing wire facilities.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease or ownership proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed, apply for provisional tax registration and request an extension. If the bank refuses to open the operating account, submit a revised board resolution appointing compliant signatories or select an alternate licensed bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Medical Device Manufacturing License and Factory Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan Food and Drug Administration (TFDA), Ministry of Health and Welfare, and local Industrial Development Bureau.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the Taiwan Food and Drug Administration for a Medical Device Manufacturing License under the QMS/QSD system, submitting the plant layout, equipment list, clean-room specifications, product technical files, and process validation data. The TFDA will conduct a GMP/QMS quality audit of the microfluidic cartridge production, reagent filling, and immunoassay analyzer assembly lines. In parallel, file factory registration with the local industrial development bureau and municipal government, and submit the environmental impact assessment and civil defense fire safety applications as outlined in the licensing chapter. Production of automated point-of-care IVD devices may commence only after all five certificates are issued and posted at the registered factory premises.
required_dossiers: Incorporation certificate and tax registration certificate
Factory QMS/GMP documentation and quality manual
Plant floor plan and clean-room classification certificate
Product technical files and performance data
Civil defense fire safety inspection report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If TFDA identifies GMP/QMS deficiencies, submit a corrective action response within the statutory 180-day period and request re-inspection. If environmental or fire permits are refused, implement engineering controls and re-apply with revised compliance evidence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Taiwan Food and Drug Administration (TFDA), Ministry of Health and Welfare; local Industrial Development Bureau, Ministry of Economic Affairs.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Manufacturing License (GMP/QMS Certificate) and Registered Factory Permit for IVD Manufacturing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration (now Ministry of Environment), Executive Yuan, Taiwan.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Initial Environmental Examination (IEE) and site-specific pollution prevention plan; a full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) report is required if monthly hazardous waste generation exceeds 50 kilograms or if chemical storage exceeds the statutory regulatory threshold.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must comply with pH 6-9, COD less than or equal to 100 mg/L, BOD less than or equal to 30 mg/L, suspended solids less than or equal to 30 mg/L, and total phosphorus less than or equal to 5 mg/L. VOC emissions from coating and reagent filling lines must be captured by local exhaust systems with control efficiency of at least 90%. Hazardous chemical and biological waste must be disposed of by a licensed contractor and tracked under the EPA manifest system. Air emissions from the analyzer assembly and clean-room HVAC systems must comply with Taiwan Air Pollution Control Act emission standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety facility inspection certificate issued by the National Fire Agency for the registered factory; structural load inspection certificate by a licensed structural engineer for equipment platforms and clean-room mezzanines; and workplace safety clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including hazardous substance exposure monitoring, personal protective equipment certification, and emergency response training records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China, exercised through provincial and municipal Tax Service Bureaus; online filing and administrative procedures are completed via the Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) portal, with VAT invoice controls through the National VAT Invoice Management System operated under Golden Tax Phase IV.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise with the State Administration for Market Regulation and obtain the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code, which is the statutory Taxpayer Identification Number for all PRC tax purposes. Step 2: Tax registration is automatically completed through the SAMR-tax authority information sharing mechanism within 30 days of issuance of the business license; no separate paper tax registration certificate is issued. Step 3: Log onto the Electronic Tax Bureau and complete new taxpayer formalities, including selection of VAT taxpayer status as small-scale taxpayer or general taxpayer, determination of VAT filing period, accounting standard confirmation, and registration for electronic invoice issuance entitlement. Step 4: Apply for a digital Tax U-Key and electronic invoice authorization so that the WFOE can issue special and ordinary VAT invoices through the National VAT Invoice Management System. Step 5: For a genuinely foreign non-resident enterprise with no permanent establishment in China, the Chinese withholding agent, or the non-resident enterprise itself where required, must complete a non-resident enterprise tax registration with the competent Tax Service Bureau and obtain a temporary non-resident TIN; the application typically requires the foreign enterprise registration certificate, the cross-border service or royalty contract, and appointment of a PRC tax representative. This SOP therefore covers both the resident WFOE and the non-resident foreign-parent scenario.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (the WFOE is a Chinese resident enterprise incorporated under PRC Company Law and is subject to enterprise income tax on worldwide income; no pass-through treatment is available).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity-classification purposes: PRC law does not provide a check-the-box election or hybrid-mismatch entity election. The WFOE may, however, elect general VAT taxpayer status if below the mandatory threshold, and may apply for High and New Technology Enterprise status to access the reduced 15% enterprise income tax rate; both are procedural or incentive elections and do not alter entity-level tax classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) of the People's Republic of China, governed by the VAT Law of the People's Republic of China effective 1 January 2026 and, for earlier periods, the Interim Regulations on VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no turnover threshold for basic tax registration because all established business entities must complete tax registration at incorporation. The mandatory VAT general-taxpayer registration threshold is RMB 5,000,000 of cumulative taxable sales over a rolling 12-month period; below that threshold the WFOE may remain a small-scale taxpayer using the simplified VAT rate of 3% (subject to temporary preferential reductions), while crossing the threshold obliges conversion to general taxpayer status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices, including ordinary, special, and fully digitalized electronic invoices, must be issued through the National VAT Invoice Management System (Golden Tax Phase IV) and transmitted in real time to the competent Tax Service Bureau. The tax authority centrally clears each invoice by assigning a unique invoice code and number, and purchasers can verify authenticity on the VAT Invoice Public Service Platform. There is no transactional fiscal stamping model; instead, invoice clearance is achieved through centralized electronic data matching, and export sales are separately flagged as zero-rated in the e-invoice system and reconciled electronically with China Customs export release data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods from mainland China, including exports to the Taiwan jurisdiction as a separate customs territory, is eligible for the 0% VAT rate and refund of attributable input VAT where all of the following conditions are met: (1) the WFOE is registered as a PRC VAT general taxpayer; (2) the manufactured IVD goods physically leave mainland China and are declared to China Customs in the WFOE's own name; (3) the export sales are supported by an export customs declaration with electronic release data; (4) the export proceeds are received and repatriated through lawful foreign-exchange channels within 180 days of the export customs declaration date; (5) the WFOE files the export tax rebate declaration through the Electronic Tax Bureau within the statutory filing period; and (6) the exported IVD goods are lawfully registered or licensed under PRC medical-device and customs export-control rules. Qualifying offshore digital services may also be zero-rated if listed in the cross-border taxable-services catalogue, but the principal export here is physical goods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: China Customs Export Goods Declaration (electronic clearance data generated through the China International Trade Single Window)
Bill of Lading, air waybill, or international road cargo transport document issued by the carrier and evidencing actual exportation
Commercial invoice and packing list issued in the name of the exporting WFOE

Bank Export Proceeds Collection Receipt (the Chinese statutory export-proceeds collection record, integrated with the SAFE Trade in Goods Foreign Exchange Monitoring System and functionally equivalent to a foreign inward remittance certificate)
Export tax rebate declaration form and the e-Tax filing acceptance receipt
Certificate of the WFOE's Unified Social Credit Code and VAT general-taxpayer registration notice
Valid IVD medical-device registration certificate and any export-specific customs license required for the microfluidic cartridges or immunoassay analyzers
SWIFT LC or TT wire payment evidence and the overseas purchase contract demonstrating the commercial substance of the cross-border trade
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the export customs declaration is false, the goods are re-imported or diverted into domestic PRC consumption without lawful procedures, or the foreign-exchange proceeds are not repatriated within 180 days without timely regulatory approval, the tax authority may disallow the zero-rating, claw back any export VAT refund already granted, and reclassify the export sale as domestic taxable supply subject to 13% VAT plus late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day. A fraudulent claim for an export tax refund is treated under the Law on the Administration of Tax Collection as a serious tax violation: the tax authority will recover the refunded amount and impose a penalty of 50% to 5 times the amount involved. Where the amount is large or the scheme is organized, criminal liability for fraudulent export tax refund under the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China may arise, with penalties including imprisonment, fines, and confiscation of property. Enhanced audit scrutiny is expected where SWIFT LC or TT payment patterns, high-risk destination markets, invoice values, or customs quantities are inconsistent with the timing and amount of foreign-exchange repatriation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China, acting under the delegation of the People's Bank of China (PBOC), with the PBOC holding ultimate monetary authority and SAFE administering all cross-border foreign exchange, FDI, trade settlement, and capital account transactiobs.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The PRC maintains a hybrid convertibility regime. Current account transactions, including trade-related payments for goods and services, are largely freely convertible after banks perform documentary authenticity verification. Capital account transactions remain controlled: inbound foreign direct investment into the WFOE is permitted under the Foreign Investment Negative List, but requires SAFE foreign exchange registration, an onshore capital account, and a bank pre-review of the capital injection contract. Received FDI can be converted into RMB through settlement under the capital account, but must be applied to bona fide business expenditures; speculative use or outbound lending is prohibited. Profit remittances are treated as current account payment of investment returns, subject to audited financial statements, corporate income tax completion or withholding certificates, board resolution, and the absence of pending SAFE penalties. The offshore Taiwan parent may not freely re-inject fungible funds after receipt; each injection must be traceable to the registered capital schedule. Currency conversion for outward remittances is conditioned on genuine transaction documents, and no full capital account liberalization exists. The WFOE should therefore structure each invoice, equity injection, and dividend declaration as a separately docketed compliance file.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China abolished forced foreign currency surrender, but 100% of export foreign currency receipts from IVD sales must be repatriated into an onshore bank account within 180 days of the export customs declaration, unless a SAFE exemption is approved for specific offshore settlement practices. No mandatory conversion ratio applies; the WFOE may retain export proceeds in a foreign currency current account or voluntarily convert them into RMB at market rates. The exporter must report each receipt through the SAFE digital foreign exchange platform and maintain the underlying customs declarations, bills of lading, commercial invoices, and packing lists for bank authenticity review.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and FDI Foreign Currency Capital Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (RMB) plus Foreign Currency Current Account
Foreign Currency Working Capital Account and Trade Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI platforms are not viable as the primary treasury or statutory capital account receptor for the China WFOE. Such EMIs are not licensed by SAFE and cannot perform FDI registration, capital verification, export surrender reporting, or onshore RMB clearing under the PRC Foreign Account regulations. PBoC and SAFE require WFOEs to maintain primary settlement relationships with licensed domestic banks that are direct participants in CNAPS, CIPS, and SWIFT correspondent rails. Fintech EMIs may be used only as ancillary collection channels for overseas distributor payments, and only if the EMI controls cross-border remittance data in compliance with PBoC rules and does not accept the WFOE's statutory equity capital. Legal constraint: offshore EMIs generally cannot offer CN domestic account numbers in the WFOE's name, and their payment aggregator status does not equal a PRC banking license.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under PBoC Customer Identification and Customer Due Diligence rules, the WFOE's statutory legal representative or a designated authorized director must generally appear in-branch for the initial account-opening interview. Remote opening may be permitted when the legal representative is outside mainland China and executes a notarized power-of-attorney witnessed by a PRC consulate or apostilled under the Hague Convention, while the authorized in-person representative and the WFOE compliance officer appear physically at the bank. Bank of China and ICBC typically require at least one physical visit by the legal representative or authorized signatory with the original notarized POA, the corporate chop, the original business license, and the SAFE registration certificate. Offshore proxy-only opening of a full-capability capital account is not standard practice. A second video interview may supplement but cannot fully replace the physical presence requirement for the capital account and trade settlement account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity in the Taiwan parent structure or the ultimate shareholders' source of funds cannot be verified sufficiently for the China bank's compliance committee.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the Taiwan parent's certificate of incorporation, complete corporate registry extract, shareholder register, organizational chart, ultimate beneficial owner passports, board resolution appointing the WFOE director, notarized source-of-funds statements from each investor, twelve months of parent bank statements, negative news and sanctions screening reports, and a sworn affidavit confirming no undisclosed nominee shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between the medical IVD business scope, the NMPA regulatory license, and the requested cross-border payment flow, including advance payments to third-party component suppliers or urgent commission payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the China Medical Device Registration Certificate for the IVD analyzers and microfluidic cartridges, business license covering ISIC 3250 medical device manufacturing, NMPA or provincial drug administration import/export filing, executed supply contracts with distributors, proforma invoices, bills of lading, customs declarations, and an itemized reconciliation explaining each third-party payable and the underlying commercial rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection is not strictly aligned with the SAFE-registered registered capital schedule, or the remittance originates from a jurisdiction or intermediary bank that is not consistent with the Taiwan parent's corporate banking profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: File the SAFE Foreign Exchange Registration Certificate for FDI, board resolution approving the capital injection, capital contribution schedule, equity subscription agreement, parent bank SWIFT MT103 evidence showing direct origination from the Taiwan parent's account, a legal opinion confirming no third-party or circular funding, and a bank-to-bank correspondent chain analysis showing no sanctioned intermediary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk personnel nexus or trade-based money laundering suspicion because biological reagent purchases, trademark royalties, and service fees travel through Hong Kong or other intermediate jurisdictions without a clear economic-substance link to the IVD production cycle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the complete contractual chain from the Taiwan parent through any Hong Kong procurement office to the WFOE, the actual airway bills and ocean bills with customs manifests, insurance certificates, inspection certificates, laboratory reagent safety data sheets, a transfer pricing study supporting royalty or service fees, and a legal opinion verifying the economic substance of each intermediate party and the absence of shell or pass-through entities.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan parent must initiate an MT103 wire transfer to the WFOE's SAFE-registered capital account at Bank of China Limited or another tier-1 domestic bank. The payment purpose code must be classified under the SAFE balance of payments transaction code for inward direct investment equity capital, corresponding to registered capital injection, and the bank must complete the foreign exchange receipt declaration form for the capital account. The bank will verify the FDI registration certificate, the capital injection schedule, the board resolution, and the equity subscription agreement before crediting the receipt as capital. After the foreign currency arrives, the WFOE may settle the funds into RMB using a real transaction declaration, and the local certified public accountant must issue a capital verification report in accordance with China's Company Law and the Administration for Market Regulation filing rules. The WFOE must then only deploy the RMB proceeds into payroll, raw materials, capex, or other permitted operating expenditures; sweeping or relending the capital to the parent is prohibited.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For settlement of raw material imports, component purchases, royalty payments, and other international trade obligations, the WFOE should use SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for open-account trade, commercial letters of credit issued by the onshore bank under MT700/MT707 for larger or risk-controlled transactions, and documentary collections under URC522 for occasional settlements where LC is not required. For RMB-denominated cross-border payments to suppliers in Taiwan and other regions, the WFOE should route through CIPS via the domestic bank with the same SAFE trade purpose code and full supporting documents: customs declarations for goods, commercial invoices, packing lists, transport documents, insurance certificates, and tax withholding vouchers for cross-border service fees. The bank will require the transaction to be reported in SAFE's trade in goods monitoring system before each debit is released, and the WFOE's treasury must maintain a rolling trade reconciliation for audit readback.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore CNY/USD deliverable forward contracts supported by genuine trade or capital-settlement exposure and governed by the NAFMII master agreement, requiring a bank credit limit and SAFE-compliant underlying transaction documentation.
Onshore foreign exchange swaps between USD and CNY for matching the WFOE's liquidity in both currencies, including trade receipts and capital injection funds, with no speculative open position.

Plain-vanilla FX options purchased by the WFOE to hedge future USD receivables or USD payables, including call options on USD/CNY for import settlements and put options for export proceeds, with the bank as the option seller and the WFOE as the premium payer only.

Cross-currency swaps for medium-term matching of the Taiwan parent's shareholder loan or working-capital exposure between CNY and USD, limited to cash flows directly related to the WFOE's approved investment or trade obligations.

Non-deliverable forwards and offshore CNY/NDF trades are not permissible for the onshore WFOE, because SAFE's real-demand principle requires actual currency delivery and an underlying trade or investment transaction; the Taiwan parent may consider offshore NDF hedges only for its own non-mainland balance-sheet exposure and must not settle them through the WFOE.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-seeking enterprise income tax annual return and settlement filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (regional tax administration in Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year WFOE, the annual return must be filed between May 1 and May 31 following the tax year; for a non-calendar fiscal year, within five months after the close of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a statutory surcharge of 3% of the unpaid assessed tax for every two-week period or fraction thereof after the deadline, capped at 30%; overdue tax also accrues daily statutory interest; if payment is not made after a 30-day demand, the case is transferred to the Administrative Enforcement Agency for compulsory execution; continued non-filing may lead to MOEA administrative dissolution and cancellation of the profit-seeking enterprise registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary shareholders' meeting and approval of statutory financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting; signed minutes, attendance records, and approved financial statements must be kept at the registered office and are subject to inspection by the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be convened within six months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year entity, on or before June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The responsible director is subject to an administrative fine of NTD 10,000 to NTD 50,000 for failure to convene on time; MOEA may order the meeting to be convened within a fixed period and, for continued default, may initiate compulsory dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of shareholder-approved financial statements and annual company registration confirmation with MOEA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Commercial Services, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after approval of the annual financial statements by the shareholders' meeting, and no later than July 15 for a calendar-year entity whose meeting is held on June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The responsible person is liable to an administrative fine of NTD 10,000 to NTD 50,000 per violation; continuing failure after MOEA's rectification order may trigger administrative strike-off, deregistration, and dissolution under Company Act Article 10.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign-invested enterprise operation report to the Investment Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC), Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the fiscal year, i.e., on or before June 30 for a calendar-year WFOE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by the deadline may result in fines under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals; repeated refusal may lead to suspension or revocation of the foreign investment approval, followed by MOEA administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner (UBO) register update and annual confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MOEA company registration online portal / commercial registration system of Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any change in shareholding, ultimate beneficial ownership, directors, supervisors, or senior managers must be filed within 15 days after the change; annual confirmation is filed together with the post-shareholders-meeting MOEA filing, due no later than July 15 for calendar-year entities, creating a maximum 30-day confirmation window after the annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or file the UBO register is a standalone violation under Company Act Article 22-1; the responsible person may be fined up to NTD 5,000,000 and ordered to rectify; continued noncompliance allows MOEA to strike off the registration and commence dissolution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent certified public accountant (CPA) audit is legally mandatory for (1) all public companies listed on TWSE/TPEx and other SEC-regulated issuers; (2) any non-public Taiwan company whose paid-in capital reaches or exceeds NTD 30,000,000, as prescribed under Company Act Article 20 and related MOEA directives; (3) banks, insurance companies, securities firms, financial holding companies, and other regulated financial institutions regardless of capital size; (4) companies applying for foreign-investment approval where the Ministry of Economic Affairs or the Investment Commission conditions the approval on audited financial statements. There is no standalone turnover or headcount threshold for a private non-public WFOE under Company Act, but if the WFOE is consolidated into a TWSE/TPEx

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: People's Republic of China Corporate Income Tax headline rate; reduction to 15% for High and New Technology Enterprise (HNTE) status; preferential effective rate for Small and Low-Profit Enterprises on qualified annual taxable income up to RMB 3 million; 100% super deduction for qualified Research and Development (R&D) expenditure; preferential 15% rate for encouraged industries in Hainan Free Trade Port and certain approved free-trade-zone programs; accelerated depreciation for manufacturing fixed assets; no patent-box regime, but IVD manufacturing R&D may qualify for HNTE and R&D super deductions if the ownership, personnel, R&D expense, and high-tech income ratio tests are satisfied.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Form A, 2017 Edition) filed electronically via the State Taxation Administration electronic tax-bureau portal (e-Tax) or the local in-charge tax authority's electronic filing system; quarterly provisional returns use Enterprise Income Tax Quarterly Return (Form A).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual Return and final payment due within five months after the tax year-end, i.e. 31 May for a calendar-year-taxpayer; quarterly provisional returns and quarterly payments due within 15 days after the end of each quarter; a non-calendar fiscal year must follow the approved accounting year and the five-month final-filing rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification and legal status: taxpayer name, Unified Social Credit Code, registered address, and tax classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The CN WFOE must be declared as a PRC tax resident enterprise. The Taiwanese non-resident shareholder must not be entered as the taxpayer of this return; shareholder identity and relationship should be disclosed separately in the Annual Related Party Transaction Report. Ensure the legal name and registered address exactly match the business license and tax registration certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year, accounting basis, and applicable tax rate selection.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select the calendar year unless a special non-calendar fiscal year has been approved. The WFOE is taxed at the 25% headline rate; any reduced HNTE or small-low-profit rate claimed must be supported by the relevant qualification certificate or income-threshold calculation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue from sales of goods and services: gross revenue from IVD immunoassay analyzers, microfluidic cartridges, after-sales service, and related ancillary income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Record revenue exclusive of Value-Added Tax (VAT). Export sales to the Taiwanese parent or other related parties must be included. All intercompany sales must reflect arm's-length pricing, and any transfer pricing adjustment in respect of the Taiwan-related transactions must be recorded in this box or the reconciliation section. Understating related-party revenue is a primary audit trigger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of main business: manufacturing cost of IVD instruments, cartridge consumables, packaging, direct materials, direct labor, and manufacturing overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The cost allocation must be supported by an inventory costing method consistent with PRC GAAP. If the WFOE purchases components from Taiwan-related suppliers, the transfer price must be tested under the Comparable Uncontrolled Price (CUP), Resale Price, Cost Plus, Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM), or Profit Split method as appropriate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling, general, and administrative expenses, including R&D expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct ordinary and necessary expenses only. Intercompany management fees, trademark royalties, technical support fees, and service charges paid or payable to the Taiwanese parent require a benefit test, valid contracts, contemporaneous documentation, and withholding tax compliance. R&D super deduction must be claimed only for qualified R&D projects with contemporaneous project records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income and expenses, including disposal gains, exchange differences, and government grants.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Examine whether any payment from or to the Taiwanese parent is a constructive dividend, capital contribution, or unapproved shareholder loan. Interest-free shareholder loans and disguised capital injections are subject to deemed-interests adjustments and may be recharacterized by the tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total accounting profit (book profit before corporate income tax).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The accounting profit must reconcile with the financial statements audited for PRC statutory purposes. If the WFOE entered into transactions with the Taiwan parent solely to reduce PRC taxable income, the accounting profit will be adjusted below in the tax-adjustment section.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment items: permanent differences, temporary differences, transfer pricing adjustments, thin-capitalization interest disallowance, and treaty-benefit disallowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-related adjustments include: disallowed interest under the thin-capitalization ratio (debt/equity 2:1 generally, 5:1 for financial institutions), recharacterized royalty payments, and reclassification of management fees lacking economic substance. Any TP adjustment made by the State Taxation Administration must be recorded here, with corresponding interest and penalty implications.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carryforward: prior-year losses applied in the current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A WFOE may carry forward qualified losses for not more than five years. Losses generated from transactions lacking commercial substance or artificial related-party arrangements may be denied. The Taiwanese shareholder cannot claim the WFOE's losses in the Taiwanese return unless an effective cross-strait tax agreement and credit mechanism applies.

The final taxable income is the base for the 25% statutory rate. The tax authority may substitute taxable income under Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law where the WFOE and the Taiwan parent or Taiwan affiliate enter into arrangements lacking reasonable commercial purpose.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax incentive reductions: HNTE 15% reduced tax computation, Small and Low-Profit preferential rate, R&D super deduction, and foreign tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Taiwanese shareholder is entitled to a reduced rate under an applicable bilateral arrangement, the benefit is not claimed in this box. The WFOE may claim only enterprise-level incentives. A foreign tax credit may be available for PRC tax paid on foreign-source income of the WFOE, but not for withholding tax on dividends distributed to Taiwanese shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed tax payable, quarterly prepayments, credits, net tax due, or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: After deducting quarterly prepayments, the balance must be settled by 31 May. The WFOE, as withholding agent, is separately obligated to withhold the 10% dividend withholding tax on any distribution resolved in favor of the Taiwanese shareholder; the final CIT return box does not offset that withholding liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under Article 62 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law ranges from RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000; late payment triggers a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax. False or fraudulent returns, understatement, or tax evasion under Article 63 subjects the taxpayer to a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax. Criminal fraud thresholds are governed by Article 201 of the Criminal Law: tax evasion exceeding RMB 50,000 and exceeding 10% of the total tax due may lead to imprisonment of up to three years; evasion of a large amount exceeding 30% of the tax due may lead to imprisonment from three to seven years, together with criminal fines. The legal representative may also face an exit ban and high-consumption restriction where tax debts remain unpaid.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on gross dividends distributed by the PRC-resident WFOE to a non-resident Taiwanese corporate shareholder under Article 37 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and Article 39 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law Implementing Regulations, unless a reduced rate is available under an effective bilateral tax arrangement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim any reduced dividend, interest, or royalty rate under a cross-strait tax arrangement, the Taiwanese shareholder must: (1) obtain a Taiwan Tax Residency Certificate from the competent Taiwan tax authority confirming status as a tax resident of Taiwan; (2) submit a Beneficial Ownership Declaration to the PRC withholding agent and in-charge tax authority; (3) evidence that the Taiwanese shareholder is not a conduit, agent, or nominee and that it has substantive business activities and core income-generating activities in Taiwan; (4) provide a copy of the cross-strait arrangement and the applicable reduced-rate article; (5) obtain an advance withholding-tax reduction approval or the tax authority's acceptance before the distribution is made; and (6) preserve board resolutions, shareholder ledgers, shareholding percentage records, bank statements, and contracts to substantiate the 25%-or-higher ownership threshold and beneficial ownership. Caution: the signed PRC-Taiwan Cross-Strait Tax Agreement may not be operative in all cases; absent an effective instrument, the WFOE must withhold the statutory 10% WHT on dividends, interest, and royalties and the Taiwanese shareholder may be unable to claim any unilateral PRC treaty benefit.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on outbound interest and royalties is also 10%, subject to VAT and surcharges on royalties and imported services. Interest paid to the Taiwanese parent must also pass the thin-capitalization and arm's-length interest tests. Royalties paid for IVD trademark or patented technology are scrutinized for beneficial ownership and economic substance; if a cross-strait tax arrangement is effective, treaty rates may be reduced to the applicable rates in the arrangement, generally conditioned on the receiving shareholder or beneficiary being the beneficial owner and on the absence of tie-in structures that constitute treaty abuse.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File must be prepared when annual related-party tangible property transfers exceed RMB 200 million; financial asset transfers exceed RMB 100 million; intangible asset ownership transfers exceed RMB 100 million; or other related-party transactions aggregate more than RMB 40 million. Master File must be prepared when annual cross-border related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion or when the enterprise is designated by the State Taxation Administration. The WFOE must also file the Annual Related Party Transaction Report with the annual CIT return whenever any related-party transaction occurs.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The PRC does not apply OECD-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as a separate statute, but the tax authorities apply a substance-over-form doctrine, the General Anti-Abuse Rule under Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law, and the beneficial ownership rules under State Taxation Administration Public Notices to deny treaty/double-taxation relief where the Taiwanese shareholder or WFOE lacks commercial substance. For the WFOE, Core Income-Generating Activities for IVD manufacturing must be performed in mainland China: product design, production, quality control, regulatory licensing, inventory management, and revenue booking should be supported by local personnel and premises. The Taiwanese parent must likewise demonstrate real business activity in Taiwan to be recognized as beneficial owner of any dividend, interest, or royalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Taiwanese investor forms the WFOE as a paper entity with no physical IVD manufacturing facility, no employees, no equipment, no core income-generating activity in mainland China, and uses a Taiwanese affiliate as a pass-through conduit for patent licensing and sales bookings, while claiming double-taxation agreement relief or understating PRC corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The in-charge tax authority may recharacterize the entire structure under Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and Article 120 of the Implementing Regulations; apply a deemed taxable income adjustment; deny the cross-strait tax treaty or arrangement benefit; impose the 10% withholding tax on the deemed dividend; impose a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05%; and assess a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax under Article 63 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law. The entity may also be listed as a serious-tax-dishonest party, triggering joint punishment including travel restrictions and public blacklisting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the legal representative who knowingly participated in the shell arrangement may have the corporate veil pierced under Article 20 of the PRC Company Law and be held jointly and severally liable for the WFOE's unpaid corporate income tax and penalties. The legal representative will face an exit-entry control measure (travel ban) for outstanding tax liabilities; assets may be frozen; and criminal liability may arise under Article 201 of the Criminal Law for tax evasion, with imprisonment of up to seven years and fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation / BEPS Base Erosion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE enters into fabricated intercompany arrangements with the Taiwanese parent: excessive management fees, inflated technical service fees, non-arm's-length prices for IVD cartridges and analyzer components, or a TNMM selection that deliberately produces the lowest taxable profit. The WFOE does not prepare contemporaneous Local File or Master File, fails to file related-party transaction forms, and uses the transfer pricing structure to strip profits out of mainland China without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The State Taxation Administration may apply Article 41 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law, make a transfer pricing adjustment, increase taxable income, add interest on the underpaid tax, and impose a penalty for failure to provide contemporaneous documentation under Article 70 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law. Fraudulent transfer pricing reporting may be treated as tax evasion under Article 63, attracting a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax and daily late-payment surcharges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the financial officer who sign the false transfer pricing documentation and related-party schedules can be subject to civil liability for the WFOE's tax adjustment when the company is unable to satisfy the liability; Chinese courts have applied the corporate-veil piercing doctrine to hold controlling shareholders personally liable; the legal representative is tagged as a tax-dishonest person and banned from leaving China; if the understatement is deliberate and large, criminal prosecution under Article 201 of the Criminal Law can result in imprisonment for three to seven years and criminal fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Disguised Dividend Distribution and Withholding Tax Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE avoids paying formal dividends by extending interest-free shareholder loans to the Taiwanese parent, capitalizing retained earnings through excessive royalty payments, or making non-commercial payments to Taiwanese affiliates; the WFOE fails to withhold the 10% dividend WHT on the economic distribution, and the Taiwanese shareholder receives profits from mainland China without paying any PRC corporate income tax at source.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may deem the shareholder loan or excessive payment to be a dividend distribution under Article 39 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law Implementing Regulations and apply Article 37 withholding tax. As withholding agent, the WFOE is liable for the unwithheld tax; Article 69 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law imposes a penalty of 50% to 300% of the amount that should have been withheld. Thin-capitalization disallowances under Article 46 and the General Anti-Abuse Rule under Article 47 may also operate to deny the interest deduction and recharacterize the transaction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve the disguised distribution and fail to discharge the withholding obligation may be personally liable for the withholding penalty if the WFOE is unable to pay. The legal representative will be subject to exit restrictions and high-consumption curbs; assets of the company and the Taiwanese parent may be attached if the corporate veil is pierced; criminal exposure includes imprisonment for tax evasion or fraud where the failure to withhold is part of a scheme to conceal income, with a maximum term of seven years and additional fines.
